newsitem.title: JAPAN: Several Japan bank shares hit new 1997 highs.
newsitem.headline: Several Japan bank shares hit new 1997 highs.

text.p: Shares in several of Japan's big banks hit new highs for calendar 1997 on Thursday morning, lifted by short-covering and index-linked buy orders, brokers said.

Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd rose past its previous high of 2,280 yen to hit 2,360 yen. As of 0053 GMT, it was up 40 at 2,320. Turnover was 3.80 million shares, making it the fifth most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
Sakura Bank Ltd climbed to a new high of 910 yen earlier in the morning before slipping to 905, or up 20 yen.
Sumitomo Bank Ltd, Fuji Bank Ltd and Sanwa Bank Ltd also hit new highs for the calendar year.
The banking sector 0#BNK.T was the second largest gaining sector on the bourse.

"The indices are rising and funds which have kept bank sector shares at low levels in their portfolios are hurrying to increase their holdings, contributing greatly to gains in the TOPIX index," a broker at a major brokerage said.
"Shareholder meetings are drawing near and there is much attention on share prices and investors feel reluctant to sell," a broker at a mid-sized brokerage said.
